label: S. 3900

latest_action.text: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 504.

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The S. 3900 bill aims to promote human rights, internet freedom, and accountability in Iran by directing the Secretary of State and federal agencies to expand uncensored internet access, support civil society and independent media, and provide cybersecurity training for Iranian citizens. The bill also requires strategies and reports regarding internet circumvention, technology deployment, human rights assistance, and the use of Near East Regional Democracy (NERD) funds, while explicitly stating it does not authorize the use of military force.

affected_groups.effect: Will have increased access to training, digital-safety tools, uncensored internet circumvention technologies, and support for documenting human rights abuses.
affected_groups.group: Iranian citizens, civil society actors, and human rights activists

affected_groups.effect: Will potentially receive grants for equipment, training, and secure communication platforms to support independent reporting.
affected_groups.group: Independent Iranian journalists and media outlets

affected_groups.effect: Required to draft updated strategies, submit congressional reports, coordinate interagency working groups, and track performance metrics.
affected_groups.group: Federal agencies (Department of State, GAO, etc.)

key_provisions: Designates the Secretary of State as the primary federal official responsible for promoting internet freedom and coordinating digital freedom initiatives in Iran.
Extends and increases authorization for the Iran Internet Freedom Grant Program through fiscal year 2030, authorizing up to $20,000,000 for each fiscal year through 2030.
Requires the Secretary of State to submit an updated comprehensive strategy on internet freedom and access to information within 120 days of enactment.

Directs the Department of State, in coordination with other federal agencies, to support the development of low-cost, scalable technologies to counter internet shutdowns, such as mesh networks and VPNs.
Requires a strategy on human rights assistance and a GAO report examining federal expenditures under the Near East Regional Democracy (NERD) account over fiscal years 2024 and 2025.

Instructs the Secretary of State to establish programs delivering cybersecurity training, digital-safety tools (such as VPNs and encrypted messaging), and educational materials to journalists and human rights defenders in Iran.
Includes a rule of construction explicitly stating that nothing in the Act authorizes the use of military force.
missing_information: Exact overall appropriations figures or total budget caps for carrying out the Act, as section 9 states funds are derived from existing amounts authorized or made available to the Department of State.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The S. 3900 bill aims to promote human rights, internet freedom, and accountability in Iran by directing the Secretary of State and federal agencies to expand uncensored internet access, support civil society and independent media, and provide cybersecurity training for Iranian citizens. The bill also requires strategies and reports regarding internet circumvention, technology deployment, human rights assistance, and the use of Near East Regional Democracy (NERD) funds, while explicitly stating it does not authorize the use of military force.
summary_detail.significance: The bill establishes formal reporting requirements, expands grant programs for internet freedom, and mandates continuous interagency strategies focused on counter-censorship and human rights support in Iran.

title: Iran Human Rights, Internet Freedom, and Accountability Act of 2026
